question: diffusion models for video generation

2006.11239.caption: The figure displays two sets of image grids: a 2x2 grid of high-resolution human faces on the left and a large 10x10 grid of diverse, low-resolution objects (such as animals, vehicles, and landscapes) on the right. It conveys the quality and variety of images generated by the model on the CelebA-HQ and CIFAR-10 datasets.

2112.10752.caption: The figure presents a comparison of image synthesis quality across three models (ours with $f=4$, DALL-E with $f=8$, and VQGAN with $f=16$) alongside an input image. Each model's output is displayed in a grid with corresponding performance metrics (PSNR and R-FID) labeled above each column. The figure conveys that lower spatial downsampling factors ($f$) lead to higher PSNR and lower R-FID, indicating superior image reconstruction and synthesis quality.

2209.14792.caption: This figure displays four rows of image sequences, labeled (a) through (d), representing video frames generated from text prompts. Each row illustrates a different visual concept—a flying superhero dog, a pile of books in sunlight, a dancing robot, and running unicorns—to demonstrate the model's ability to produce coherent motion and high-quality video generation.

2103.00020.caption: The figure illustrates the CLIP framework through three panels: (1) a contrastive pre-training process showing an image and text being passed through respective encoders to produce a matrix of similarity scores between $N$ image and text embeddings; (2) the creation of a dataset classifier by passing label text through a text encoder to generate class embeddings; and (3) zero-shot prediction where an image is encoded and compared against the previously generated class embeddings. The diagram uses boxes to represent data (images, text, and matrices) and encoders, with arrows indicating the flow of information through the model components.

2210.02303.caption: The figure displays a grid of eight video frames showing autumn leaves falling onto a blue lake. The frames progress from a scene of scattered leaves to a sequence where the leaves coalesce to form the text "IMAGEN VIDEO."

2304.08818.caption: The figure displays two rows of video frame sequences generated from text prompts. The top row shows three sequences of a horse in a Van Gogh style and a dog wearing VR goggles, while the bottom row shows a sequence of an animated oil painting of a train and a real-world driving scene.

2204.03458.caption: The figure depicts a 3D U-Net architecture consisting of a sequence of colored rectangular blocks connected by arrows, representing a downsampling encoder path followed by an upsampling decoder path. The blocks are labeled with dimensions in the format of frames $\times$ height $\times$ width $\times$ channels, and curved arrows indicate concatenation skip connections from the encoder blocks to the corresponding decoder blocks. The diagram conveys the flow of a noisy video $\mathbf{z}_t$, conditioning $\mathbf{c}$, and log SNR $\lambda_t$ through a space-time factorized processing pipeline to produce an output $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_\theta$.

2010.02502.caption: The figure displays two sequences of directed nodes, $x_3$ through $x_0$, connected by arrows to represent probabilistic graphical models. The left model shows a Markovian diffusion process with sequential arrows between adjacent nodes, while the right model shows a non-Markovian inference process where nodes are connected by both sequential arrows and dashed arrows representing conditional distributions $q(x_3|x_2, x_0)$ and $q(x_2|x_1, x_0)$.

2604.15911.caption: The figure consists of three bar charts showing trends in accelerated sampling algorithms. The left chart shows the proportion of literature across different methods, with "Step Distillation" being the most prevalent at 41.2%; the middle chart displays the annual publication count for various specific algorithms from 2022 to 2026, showing a significant peak in 2025; and the right chart compares the growth of paper counts for "only video," "only image," and "both" tasks over the same period.

2603.09721.caption: The figure illustrates the architecture of FrameDiT, transitioning from a high-level block diagram of a Diffusion Transformer to three detailed block configurations: (a) Local, (b) Global, and (c) Global-Local Hybrid. The diagrams use colored boxes to represent functional components like AdaLN, Attention/Matrix Attention, MLP, and Scale, connected by arrows to show data flow. The figure conveys how the proposed "Global" method replaces standard attention with Matrix Attention for frame-level modeling and how the "Global-Local Hybrid" combines both attention types for unified spatio-temporal modeling.

2601.05966.caption: The figure consists of a grid of six sample video frames generated from text prompts. These images depict various scenes, including an astronaut riding a horse, a person on a motorcycle, a panda drinking coffee, a dog behind a drum kit, and the Eiffel Tower. The figure conveys the model's ability to generate high-fidelity and visually diverse video content.

2603.17398.caption: This diagram illustrates a Latent Diffusion Model architecture consisting of a Pixel Space, a Latent Space, and a Condition module. The pipeline shows video frames ($x$) being encoded into latent space ($z_0$) via an encoder ($\mathcal{E}$), undergoing a diffusion process to reach $z_\tau$, and being decoded back to $\hat{x}$ via a decoder ($\mathcal{D}$). The Denoising U-Net within the latent space is composed of Down, Mid, and Up blocks, each containing ResNet, Spatial Transformer, and Temporal Attention layers, with the latter being "adaptive" in the Up Block and "global" in the others.

2605.21042.caption: The figure presents a comparison of video sequences generated by the "Original" model and the "DVG" model, organized into two main panels. The left panel shows a sequence of frames of a woman drinking from a bottle, while the right panel shows two sets of sequences depicting a garden path and a cityscape. The figure conveys that the DVG method, when used with distillation at 18× speedup, produces video results visually consistent with the original model.

2602.03747.caption: The figure consists of several panels comparing video generation quality across different rollout lengths. The top panel shows qualitative sequences of frames from baseline models that rapidly degrade into color distortions, contrasted with the "Ours" sequence which maintains visual stability, alongside a line graph plotting FID scores against rollout length to quantitatively demonstrate lower error accumulation. The bottom panel displays qualitative results of the proposed model applied to diverse scenarios, including RealEstate10K, Minecraft, and UE Engine, showing stable video generation up to the 256th frame.
